brief: 011 C (play the Handover: HUD and action cards)
tool: Codex CLI image tool: python3 ~/Projects/the-suborned/workbench/Tools/Concept/codex_image.py (codex exec; ChatGPT plan; cost 0 per image; no Runware). The tool appends ' Leave clear margin around every figure: nothing cropped at the head or feet.' to every prompt and picks its own size.

style_contract.used: concept_prompt era, city, avoid, rule (the interface prompts open with the era line, the Streamline Moderne/Googie city materials and the avoid list)

deviations_from_the_style_contract: concept_prompt.avoid lists 'text, signage lettering or words' and rules.all says 'no text in the image': lifted for HUD concepts, because a price card has to carry strings. Every prompt quotes the strings exactly; spec.html and the spec renders, not the generated pictures, are the authority for every string.
concept_prompt.era is for places, objects and machines: used here for the interface as an object and machine.
No people are drawn (the portrait slot is an empty hatched silhouette), so the people rules (no era date) are not engaged; round 1 drew a period nurse, which is why round 2 forbids a face.

base_frame.note: Latch's play view at 17:00 (mission 0:00 = 17:00, mission.json clock.startsAt, provisional), Inez p-cafe-11 at the café door; same camera as people-0900-cafe.png. Ground scale measured on the frame: the 19.6 m fountain ring is 707 px, so 36.1 px/m; characters 44-49 px.

rulebook.note: Keel's rulebook was still growing while this ran (cell, security, perception tables landed during the work); the fields cited are in the file at this hash.

people_export.note: Inez p-cafe-11 (Idealist, debt, server, Corner café, 12:00-18:00), guard p-records-office-02 Ulrich Sandvik (Mercenary, debt, door, 09:30-17:30).

Colour rules: interface colours are ivory #eee9da, cream #f7f4ec, deep teal #1f6c67, seafoam #72b5a7, ink teal #17302f, chrome grey, a brass hairline #99784d, and one highlight, turquoise #1cb9c6, used only for the selected item and for planned previews. No amber, no violet, no orange, no gold surfaces and no red anywhere, with one exception: a refused marker is a tiny round dark display window holding a tiny red slashed-circle pictogram. Text rule: use only the exact words and numbers quoted in this prompt, spelled exactly; no other words, no logos, no watermark. Where a label is not quoted, draw a small pictogram instead. Pictograms: coin = cash; stopwatch = time; fingerprint = Trail; beacon lamp = Alert. Direction C, 'Case file': the interface is the city's own paper. Records are physical in this world (microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic-tube carriers, stamped forms), so the cell keeps its case on the city's own cards. Cards are cream-ivory card stock with a seafoam edge band, printed in ink teal, drawn flat and crisp. (1) Down the right edge, a tall pinned aperture card (a punch card with a clipped top-left corner), about 25% of the band wide: a rectangular microfilm window at the upper left holding a portrait window holding only a pale empty head-and-shoulders silhouette under diagonal hatching, with no face, no hair and no clothes drawn (nothing about her is learned yet); a row of exactly four small holes along the top, every one covered by a seafoam sticker (nothing is learned yet); printed header "Inez Bermudez" and "Server · Corner café · 12:00–18:00"; printed form fields, each covered by a hatched redaction bar: "Routine", "Need", "Temperament"; a section "Known" (typed line: "Works the café door, 12:00–18:00"), a section "Suspected" (a typed line on a diagonal-hatch ground: "In debt (briefing)"), a section "Planned" (a turquoise dotted-outline slip clipped to the card: "Watch · Scout · done 0:52"). (2) Under the aperture card, a clipped order slip like a pneumatic-tube carrier form, headed "Fixer · Turn", with four approach rows, each with a perforated tear-off price docket of four boxes (coin, stopwatch, fingerprint, beacon). Because her temperament is not known yet, every outcome is an unstamped dotted ring holding a question mark "?" in place of a rubber stamp. Row 1, bright: "Ask cold", "$0", "25 s", "+1", "0". Rows 2, 3 and 4 are dimmed because they are locked, each with a small padlock and a short hint, but their numbers stay readable: Row 2: "Pay", "$70,000" with a tiny line "+$20,000 ?", "50 s", "+2", "0", hint "Watch first". Row 3: "Help", "$40,000" with a tiny line "+1 Help ?", "50 s", "+1", "0", hint "Listen first". Row 4: "Pressure", "$0", "35 s", "+3" with a tiny line "+1 T ?", "0", hint "Listen first". A footer strip: "Purse $100,000". (3) Across the top, a long film strip with sprocket holes along both edges serving as the timeline, from "0:00" to "8:00", with punched notches at the event times labelled "3:10" (a hatched notch), "5:30", "5:40", "5:50", "6:10", "8:00", a solid short bar from 0:00 to 0:52 and a turquoise dotted bar right after it, and a turquoise slider marker at 0:20; at its left a dark dot-matrix window "0:20", a round chrome pause button and a button "Next event" with the line "3:10 Rival car parks"; at its right four stamped boxes in a row: coin "$100,000", fingerprint "0", exactly four unlit lamps "Routine", a slim track of seven notches with a marker on the middle notch "Neutral". (4) Bottom left: four filing tabs in a row "1 Scout" (with a line "Watch 0:32"), "2 Fixer" (pulled up and outlined in turquoise), "3 Tech", "4 Enforcer", each with a role pictogram and four tiny health pips; role pictograms: Scout binoculars, Fixer a telephone handset, Tech a tape reel, Enforcer a closed fist; none of them a shield.
